patch.value: The only two flags that make a read cheap are the only two whose closed value domain no refusal and no help text ever names

Thirteen of fifteen closed value domains teach an agent the legal set at the moment it guesses wrong. The two exceptions are exactly the two flags whose entire purpose is to reduce the number of tokens a command emits, so the only two levers that make pm cheap are the only two an agent cannot learn to use without reading our source.

Measured live on 2026-08-01 at 2026.8.1 by passing a deliberately invalid value to each flag and reading the refusal:

Domains that ARE enumerated in the refusal, complete and untruncated: list --type (11 types), list --priority (0..4), list --format (5 encodings), create positional type (11 plus a schema add-type hint), update --severity (4), update --confidence (integer range plus 4 names), update --priority (5 numbers and 5 names with their meanings), update --dep kind (all 15 spellings), update --risk (4), search --format (3), graph subcommand (all 16), schema add-status --role (9 roles), get --depth (4).

Domains that are NOT enumerated: 
- list --fields BOGUS returns "Unknown list --fields value(s): BOGUS" with three worked examples and no legal set. The recovery bundle echoes provided_fields "--fields" and stops. The real domain is at least the 24 keys that list --full --json projects.
- list --for BOGUS returns a single nearest-match guess ("Did you mean triage?") and the instruction "Use a declared list intent", whose own Examples block points at pm --help and pm COMMAND --help. There are exactly six declared intents across five commands (context orient, context handoff, get inspect, list triage, next execute, search discover) and no surface renders that set.

The help surface does not close either gap, and for --fields it actively misleads: pm list --help renders "Render custom comma-separated list fields (mutually exclusive with --compact/--brief/--full; valid: --fields id,title)". The word "valid" introduces what is an example, so a reader who trusts the help concludes the domain has two members. pm list --help renders --for as "Apply a declared context intent projection" with no domain at all.

Consequence, and why this belongs to the cost programme rather than to error-message polish: an agent that cannot learn the projection vocabulary falls back to the default or to --full, which is the single most expensive form the command has. Measured on this tracker at 2026.8.1, plain list --json is 74,457 bytes; the same query under --for triage --token-budget 3000 is 15,164 bytes. The lever exists, it works, and it is undiscoverable.

Scope fence. This is value-domain reachability for flags whose domain is closed and known at the failure site. It is not the subcommand-token contract (pm-185870), not the unknown-option suggester or same-command flag hints (pm-gdi7), not the cross-command flag hint truncation (pm-yqe0mo), and not the projection mechanism itself (pm-cxr0jb, which works). It is the discovery half of the flag lexicon that pm-fs8q9x governs.

Proposed resolution: derive both domains from the contract table that already holds them, render them in the refusal envelope untruncated alongside the nearest-match suggestion, render them in the help text for the flag, and add a conformance check that fails the build when any flag with a contract-declared closed domain refuses a value without naming that domain.

A refusal on any flag with a contract-declared closed domain renders that domain in full, untruncated, in both the human and the json envelope; list --fields BOGUS names every projectable field for that command, and the same holds for every command in the list family plus get and search; list --for BOGUS names all declared intents for that command rather than a single nearest-match guess, and the same holds for context, get, next and search; Help text for --fields and --for renders the domain rather than an example, and the word valid never precedes a proper subset; A conformance check fails the build when a flag with a contract-declared closed domain refuses a value without naming the domain, with a negative control proving the check can fail
